The island has a northeast—southwest orientation, an area of about 150,000 km², and its shape and location correspond to the South Island of New Zealand. The legend shows cities, rivers and lakes, mountain peaks, highways, railways, national parks, etc.; the mountains on the island mainly run longitudinally along the west—central part. Reasoning: The question stem asks to explain the difference that the western side of this island is dominated by animal husbandry and the eastern side is dominated by planting agriculture, and gives the prompt “related to illumination conditions.” The South Island of New Zealand is affected by the prevailing westerlies. The western side is the windward slope, with much overcast and rainy weather, clouds and fog, and less sunshine; the eastern side is located on the leeward slope of the mountains, with less precipitation, clouds, and fog, more sunny days, and longer sunshine duration, which is more favorable for planting agriculture. Therefore, another main factor forming this agricultural difference is sunshine duration.
